incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: 02:11 UTC - serving-runtime reports a spike of CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS + OOMs in gpu-pool-us-east-1a. ~12 pods crashed/restarted in the last 7m. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (large-context models), /v1/embeddings. Auto-fallback engaged for some tenants. Paging + kernel logs attached to alert.
Alice: ack — I'm on it. I can see the restart loop on node gpu-us-e1a-17 and 18. Dumping pod list now.
Alice: pods affected (short): r-runtime-embed-7f4c, r-runtime-chat-9b2d, r-runtime-gen-2a1c, r-runtime-quant-5e8f — all on gpu-us-e1a-17/18/22
Bob: any dmesg/kernel oops lines? suspecting pagewalk or GPU driver fault.
Alice: paste of dmesg from gpu-us-e1a-17:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID: 4321, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568012] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request at ffff8000abcd1234
[ 1234.568200] printk: gpu_pagewalk: misaligned address at 0x00007fffaabbccdd
[ 1234.568377] audit: type=1701 audit(1615900000.123:45): auid=4294967295 uid=0 gid=0 ses=4294967295
```
Bob: OK that looks like a misaligned pagewalk / deviceaddr translation fault — matches prior kernel/driver race we've seen. Could be triggered by specific model quantization path + batching.
Carla: confirm: we rolled kernel-driver nv-kmod v470.82 -> v470.102 on that pool yesterday for PCI fix. Might be a regression. Also saw increased continuous-batching window in config for the routes hitting these nodes.
Eve: support note: we have ~15 customer incidents opened in the last 10m, mainly high-latency or 5xx on embeddings. Some tenants auto-fell back to CPU (higher latency). CS is preparing customer-facing message.
Bob: mitigation plan (short):
- cordon + drain affected nodes to prevent restarts spreading
- enable route-level fallback (route to cpu-pool or smaller model variant)
- reduce batching window and disable continuous KV caching temporarily
- scale up dedicated cpu fallback pool and re-route traffic
We should avoid kernel changes live unless we can repro on a test node.
Alice: executing cordon/drain now for gpu-us-e1a-17/18:
```
# cordon
kubectl cordon gpu-us-e1a-17
kubectl cordon gpu-us-e1a-18
# safe drain (evict pods to fallback nodepool)
kubectl drain gpu-us-e1a-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
kubectl drain gpu-us-e1a-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
Alice: cordon done on 17/18. Drains in progress — eviction succeeded for most pods, 3 pods stuck (long mmap). Investigating.
Bob: I'll flip routing policy to prefer cpu-fallback for /v1/embeddings and set model.variant=fallback-small for high-queue tenants. Also will set batching.max_window=32 -> 8.
Carla: I'll pull NVML and kernel oops logs from the drained nodes and start a repro job on an isolated test node with same kernel/driver + model workload.
Frank: on-call handover incoming in 25m — please summarize current state for me to pick up.
Alice: handoff summary for @Frank:
- Incident: CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS + OOMs caused by misaligned pagewalk/deviceaddr faults on kernel-driver combo v470.102 on gpu-us-e1a pool.
- Impact: ~12 pods crashed, affecting /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings for ~8% of traffic in us-east region. Some tenants auto-fell back to CPU with increased latency.
- Actions taken: cordoned/draining nodes gpu-us-e1a-17/18, routing switched to cpu-fallback for embeddings, batching window reduced, scaled up cpu-fallback pool (+3 nodes), CS notified, logs collected at /run/logs/incidents/3812001111
- Next steps for oncall: monitor for repeat crashes, validate logs from test repro, coordinate with infra for possible roll-back of nv-kmod if repro confirmed. If recurs on other nodes, consider regional capacity shift.
Bob: small config snippets I'm pushing now (rolling):
```
route-config set /v1/embeddings fallback_pool=cpu-fallback
model-config set --name default variant=fallback-small
runtime-config set batching.max_window=8
```
Eve: customer comms drafted — will send to affected customers in 10m. ETA for mitigation ~20-30m, will update.
Carla: repro job started on test-gpu-01 with exact kernel/driver and the same model workload (quantized 8-bit + long context). Capturing nvme/pci traces + nvml.
Bob: if repro succeeds, we'll need infra to prepare a rollback of nv-kmod or a driver hotfix. Carla — can you attach the repro trace to a pagedebug ticket and escalate to kernel team?
Carla: yes — creating ticket KERN-2482 and attaching the tarball. Also enabling kernel livepatch telemetry.
Alice: status update 02:45 UTC — drains finished, traffic is stable on cpu-fallback for affected routes, error rates back down to baseline for most customers. Two tenants still seeing elevated 5xx (debugging).
Frank: taking over now. I'll keep the cordons in place until we have a low-risk plan. I'll own the next 60m and coordinate rollback decision if repro confirms.
Bob: FYI I'll schedule a canary of driver rollback on one non-critical node after lunch window; will coordinate with infra.
Eve: CS sent initial notice. Draft posted: "We're investigating a GPU driver-related issue affecting inference in us-east. We're routing traffic to CPU fallback to reduce errors. We will update in 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:
Alice: adding automation notes to the incident ticket: disable continuous-batching automation when driver errors detected, and a postmortem checklist.
incident-bot: Incident 3812001111 - ongoing, severity=P2, incident_channel=#incidents, runbook=/runbooks/gpu-driver-pagewalk. Updates will be appended here.
Alice: prepping full post-incident logs and timeline for retrospective once incident is resolved. :memo:
